veranderings.blok: 'n Dier hang van sy mense af
veranderings.voor: kan nie vir haar eie kos
veranderings.rede: 'vir' before the object of 'koop' is colloquial; 'self' matches the dog sentence before it and carries the same meaning.
'verantwoordelik' takes 'vir', so an infinitive needs the anticipating 'daarvoor'; the bare 'verantwoordelik om' follows English.
'volmaak' can also be read as 'perfect'; 'volgooi' is the usual verb for filling a water bowl.
'skoonhou' is a compound verb written as one word, like 'skoonmaak' in the sentence before.

veranderings.voor: Dit val minder op. Tog ly die dier ook.
veranderings.na: Dit val minder op, maar die dier ly tog ook.
veranderings.rede: Joins two very short sentences into one contrast for better flow; the comma before 'maar' is required because each part has its own subject and verb.

veranderings.blok: As jy sien 'n dier word sleg behandel
veranderings.na: om die slegte behandeling te keer
veranderings.rede: 'dit' directly follows 'die dier' and can be read as stopping or heading off the animal itself; naming what is stopped removes the ambiguity.
'Laat ... in hulle eie plek' is a literal English rendering; 'laat ... met rus' is the Afrikaans idiom for leaving an animal alone and fits the next sentence.

veranderings.na: is een van die plekke waar
veranderings.rede: 'is een plek waar' copies English 'is one place where'; Afrikaans says 'een van die plekke waar'.
